subject: Compute fabric fit for Nebula dedicated pilot
messages:
From: Dr. Aaron Hale <aaron.hale@nebulatx.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Moreno <lisa.moreno@nebulatx.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial compute profile and throughput targets

Priya,

Thanks for the intro call yesterday. We pulled together the traffic profile and an initial set of goals (attached). High level:
- Primary LLM workload: clinical summarization + long-context retrieval-augmented generation. Average prompt ~250 tokens, expected generation ~750 tokens (so ~1k tokens per call).
- Peak ingestion bursts from batch jobs arrive as sporadic spikes (~10–15 min windows) that can double call rate.
- Target SLO: p95 end-to-end inference <= 1200 ms for the user-facing path.
- Expected initial pilot traffic: 800–1,500 calls/min peak (13–25 calls/sec).
- Prefer a dedicated pool (for data separation) and we want 2–3x headroom for marketing and forecast variability.

Can you share a recommended deployment profile (GPU types/skus, approximate tokens/sec capacity, suggested headroom, and an estimated monthly committed footprint we should budget for)? Attached is our profile workbook: nebula_compute_profile.xlsx

Also, quick question: do you recommend KV-prefix caching for our retrieval patterns? We have a fair amount of repeated contexts.

Appreciate any modeling you can share prior to the follow-up with our infra team next Wednesday.

—Aaron
Dr. Aaron Hale
CTO, Nebula Therapeutics
aaron.hale@nebulatx.com
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-03-29T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial compute profile and throughput targets

Aaron — thanks for the workbook and the clear targets. We've looped in Ben and Karthik to run a short model-of-record so we can present a concrete capacity proposal ahead of next Wednesday.

Two quick clarifications that will change the numbers:
1) When you say "batch bursts" — are these arriving as many concurrent short requests (many clients simultaneously) or as fewer, long-running single requests? That changes batching efficiency assumptions.
2) Do we have a rough distribution of cacheable prefixes (any % of calls that are exact repeats)? If you can add a column in the workbook for "expected prefix-repeat %" that will help our KV hit modeling.

We'll circulate a recommended compute fabric (latency-first and cost-first options), tokens/sec per-slab, and a suggested committed footprint + 2x headroom variant. Expect a draft before EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-30T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial compute profile and throughput targets

(Forwarding Aaron's profile — internal thread to capture model assumptions and recommendation.)

Ben / Karthik — see Aaron's traffic sketch. I ran an initial set of assumptions below; please sanity-check and add your numbers. We'll fold into the external proposal.

Assumptions (baseline)
- Model family: Llama-3-13B, distilled/config tuned for clinical summarization. We will propose two runtime variants: FP16 on H100 (latency-first) and 4-bit quantized on A100-class for cost-optimized.
- Average tokens per call: 1,000 (250 prompt + 750 gen).
- Peak calls/sec (pilot): 25 cps (1,500 calls/min).
- Effective batching efficiency: 55% for user-facing requests (mix of interactive + batching), 80% for scheduled batch windows.
- Prefix/KV cache hit: base case 25% (reduces generation tokens by ~35% for cached calls).

Modeling results (back-of-envelope):
- H100 (FP16) single-VM slab (4x H100 effective concurrency topology): ~9,000 tokens/sec sustained for interactive workloads at p95 target ~450–600 ms (with warm KV cache).
- A100 (4-bit quantized) single-VM slab (8x A100 fractional share): ~5,500 tokens/sec sustained, p95 700–900 ms.

Capacity math (targeting pilot peak 25 cps -> 25,000 tokens/sec nominal):
- With 25% KV hit and 55% batching efficiency, net tokens/sec demand drops to ~13,500 tps equivalent of heavy compute.
- H100 option: need ~2 slabs (2 x 9,000 = 18,000 tps) to cover demand + comfortable headroom. Add 25% headroom => 3 slabs.
- A100 quantized option: need ~3 slabs (3 x 5,500 = 16,500 tps) + 25% headroom => 4 slabs.

Recommendation (pilot):
- Latency-first: 3 H100 slabs (dedicated) configured with KV prefix caching enabled for clinical templates, target p95 <= 600 ms, pilot committed footprint: 3 slabs.
- Cost-first: 4 quantized-A100 slabs with higher batching thresholds and aggressive prefix caching, target p95 <= 900 ms, pilot committed footprint: 4 slabs.

Operational notes (important for SLO fit):
- Warmup lanes: pre-warm 1 slab during the daily morning ramp and keep 1 slab on standby to absorb spike windows. We expect cache warming to reduce observed tail latency by ~20% after 15–30 minutes.
- Burst policy: auto-burst to host pool with overflow to lower-cost quantized variants if saturated; recommend a fallback policy in the canary to avoid 5xx spikes.
- Monitoring: token-level tracing + p95/p99 by route and by model variant. We should instrument a 2-week regression suite to watch output quality after quantization.

Costs rough estimate (monthly committed):
- 3 H100 slabs pilot: ballpark $XXk/month committed (we'll produce real $ numbers in the external doc).
- 4 A100 slabs pilot: ~40–55% lower committed compute cost but higher latency tail risk.

Ben/Karthik: fill gaps (precise tokens/sec per slab, realistic p95 under mixed traffic, and solid monthly figures). I'll fold into the pilot proposal and send to Aaron.

—Priya

Subject: Re: Initial compute profile and throughput targets

Aaron — thanks again for the workbook and the clarifications on burst shape (very helpful). We've completed the modeling and attached a concise pilot proposal (redwood_dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf). Key recommendations in plain language:

1) Pilot footprint (what we'll reserve)
- Latency-first track (recommended if p95 <= 1200 ms is a hard req): reserve 3 H100 slabs (dedicated). Expected sustained capacity: ~24k tokens/sec usable for interactive workloads with KV warm; estimated p95 ~450–650 ms under mixed load and the burst profile you described.
- Cost-first track (recommended if you can accept higher p95): reserve 4 A100 quantized slabs. Expected sustained capacity: ~22k tokens/sec with stronger batching; estimated p95 ~750–900 ms.

2) Headroom and safety margins
- We recommend starting with 3:1 headroom on client-facing routes (pilot configured conservative), which maps to the slab counts above after factoring KV hits and batching.
- Warm lanes: keep one slab hot for quick ramp; configure a 15–30 minute cache warm window for template-heavy flows.

3) Operational plan & timeline
- Week 1: Provision dedicated pilot pool, deploy model variants, run synthetic ramp.
- Week 2: Controlled customer traffic + telemetry collection; iterate batching/quantization knobs.
- Week 3: Review SLOs and decide on commit sizing for GA.

Next steps for us:
- We attached the proposal and a Drive doc with the full tokens/sec math. If this looks reasonable, can we schedule 30 minutes tomorrow with your infra lead to lock on the pilot commit and calendarize the provision window?

Links / attachments:
- Proposal: redwood_dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf
- Drive math: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nebula-dedicated-proposal
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/NEB-2027-PILOT

If you prefer, we can also run a short smoke test on Redwood Hosted to validate latency assumptions before we provision dedicated hardware.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning on a pilot cadence.

Best,
